dedupe_keys.name: recovus agent based model of post disaster household recovery

description: RecovUS is a spatial agent-based model that simulates whether homeowners repair or rebuild, wait, or sell and relocate after a disaster. It represents financial conditions, comparing repair and rent costs with resources such as National Flood Insurance payouts, FEMA housing assistance, SBA disaster loans, liquid assets and HUD CDBG-DR funds, and community conditions, where each household depends on the restoration of infrastructure, neighbours or community assets in its perceived neighbourhood; the model was presented using data on Staten Island, New York, after Hurricane Sandy in 2012. It was developed by S. Moradi with A. Nejat and published in the Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation in October 2020. Version 1.0.0 (July 2020) is available as free NetLogo code from the CoMSES library under the MIT licence. Caveats: the release is not peer reviewed by CoMSES, has no DOI and has not been updated since 2020. It supports simulation of how infrastructure restoration drives household recovery for recovery planning; a related record is the CHIME hurricane evacuation agent-based model.
name: RecovUS, agent-based model of post-disaster household recovery
